manifest.name: @local/dsh-tinyfish-mcp
manifest.description: Runs dsh's own web_search and web_fetch on TinyFish's free search and fetch APIs.

bundle.text:
# TinyFish as the backend of dsh's own web tools.
#
# `web-tinyfish` registers TinyFish on the `ctx.web` capability seam. The shipped
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web` plugin keeps owning the model-facing `web_search`
# and `web_fetch` tools, so their names, parameter schemas, descriptions and
# output rendering are exactly the official ones — only the search and fetch
# calls go to TinyFish's free Search & Fetch APIs.
#
# The `web` row below selects the TinyFish provider for both capabilities. No MCP
# server is mounted: everything TinyFish gives away for free is search and fetch,
# which these two official tools already cover, and no tool name gets a namespace
# prefix.
#
# The API key is read at activation time from $DSH_HOME/tinyfish.key (mode 600);
# it never appears in this file.
#
# `name` is a package subpath, resolved from the profile that installs this
# bundle (the bundle itself lives in that profile's node_modules), so nothing
# here depends on where the repository was cloned. `install.mjs` writes an
# absolute file:// URL instead, because it patches a profile from a checkout.
- insert:
    - id: web-tinyfish
      name: '@local/dsh-tinyfish-mcp/provider/index.mjs'
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: tinyfish
    fetchProvider: tinyfish

readme.text:
**dsh keeps its own web_search and web_fetch; TinyFish answers them, free.**

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Copy this, replace the key, and hand it to a dsh agent in **Creator mode** (创造模式). That preset is
made for changing the harness itself; any agent that can run shell commands works too. It installs,
checks, and tells you what happened.

```text
Install TinyFish as the free backend of this machine's dsh web tools. Keep the official web_search /
web_fetch tools exactly as they are: do not remove, disable or replace tool-web.

Key: sk-tinyfish-xxxx

Get a free key at <https://agent.tinyfish.ai/api-keys>, then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gg686-jkl/dsh-tinyfish.git
cd dsh-tinyfish
node install.mjs --key sk-tinyfish-xxxx
```

No git (usual on a phone):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codeload.github.com/gg686-jkl/dsh-tinyfish/tar.gz/refs/heads/main | tar xz
cd dsh-tinyfish-main && node install.mjs --key sk-tinyfish-xxxx
```

Restart dsh and open a **new session**. Search and fetch now go through TinyFish.

**Do the tools change?** No. `web_search` / `web_fetch` keep the official names, parameters, descriptions
and output format. This project only registers TinyFish as the `ctx.web` provider, so the model sees the
same tools as before.

**What does it cost?** Nothing, and no card is needed. TinySearch allows 30 requests/min and 500/hour;
TinyFetch allows 1,000 URLs/day. DeepSeek's Search & Fetch APIs bill $0.75 per 1,000 requests each.

**What about browser automation or deep research?** TinyFish charges for those, so they are not mounted
by default. `node install.mjs --key … --with-mcp` adds them as `mcp__tinyfish__*` tools.

**Why not just use the TinyFish MCP server for everything?** Its tools get namespaced
(`mcp__tinyfish__search`) and use different schemas, so a model that knows `web_search` has to relearn
them. With the official tools, nothing changes for the model.

**Does it work on the dsh-go Android app?** Yes. Same commands, no dependencies.

**Already installed the old MCP-only version?** Run `install.mjs` again; it upgrades the old block in
place.

- Requires dsh ≥ 0.2, and nothing else to install.
- The key lives in `$DSH_HOME/tinyfish.key` (mode 600) and never enters YAML.
- Your profile points at this directory, so keep it where you cloned it. If you move it, re-run
  `node install.mjs --force`.
- Need TinyFish's advanced fetch parameters (`format`, CSS selectors, 10 URLs at once) or automation and
  research in the same session? Use `--with-mcp`; TinyFish bills those per use.
